title: Nouns 1: The Base Form and Three Genders
titleRussian: Существительные 1: Начальная форма и три рода
description: Every Russian noun has a fixed gender, and you can almost always read it straight off the last letter of the dictionary form (the nominative). Hard consonant signals masculine; -а or -я signals feminine; -о or -е signals neuter.
descriptionRussian: У каждого русского существительного есть род, и обычно его видно по последней букве начальной (словарной) формы. Твёрдый согласный — мужской род; -а или -я — женский; -о или -е — средний.
intro: Russian has no "a" or "the", but it kept something English dropped centuries ago: every noun carries a gender, and that gender decides the shape of almost every word standing next to it. The good news is that you rarely have to guess. For most nouns, the last letter of the dictionary form tells you outright. This lesson teaches you to read that letter. The five that follow build the rest of the noun on top of it.
rules: The nominative case (именительный падеж) is the base, dictionary form of a noun. It is the form used for the subject of a sentence, and the form that answers кто? (who?) for people and animals or что? (what?) for things and ideas. Every other case is a change made on top of this form.
Russian sorts every noun into one of three genders: masculine (мужской род), feminine (женский род), or neuter (средний род). A noun's gender is fixed; it does not change with context.
Masculine: nouns whose nominative ends in a hard consonant. Examples: дом, журнал, телефон, брат, город, стол.
Feminine: nouns whose nominative ends in -а or -я. Examples: книга, школа, мама, машина, песня, неделя, кухня.
Neuter: nouns whose nominative ends in -о or -е. Examples: окно, письмо, молоко, утро, море, поле, солнце.
examples: Это журнал. (This is a magazine.) Журнал ends in a hard consonant, so it is masculine.
Брат дома. (My brother is home.) Брат ends in a hard consonant, so it is masculine.
Книга на столе. (The book is on the table.) Книга ends in -а, so it is feminine.
Песня красивая. (The song is beautiful.) Песня ends in -я, so it is feminine.
Окно открыто. (The window is open.) Окно ends in -о, so it is neuter.
Море далеко. (The sea is far away.) Море ends in -е, so it is neuter.

tables.title: Reading Gender from the Nominative Ending

items.explanation: Дом ends in the hard consonant -м. Hard consonant signals masculine.

items.hint: What vowel does the word end in?
items.explanation: Книга ends in -а. Both -а and -я are feminine endings.
Окно ends in -о. Both -о and -е are neuter endings. Hard consonants are masculine; -а and -я are feminine; -о and -е are neuter.

items.hint: Who is doing the reading? The subject of a Russian sentence is always in the nominative, the base form.
items.explanation: The subject of a sentence stands in the nominative case. Мама is the nominative form.

items.hint: After «Это X», what form does X take?
items.explanation: «Это X» is the textbook 'this is X' construction. The noun after Это stays in the nominative, its citation form. Песня is the nominative.

items.hint: What is the subject of the sentence? The subject takes the nominative.
items.explanation: Окно is the subject and therefore takes the nominative. The neuter short-form adjective открыто agrees with it ('the window is open'), which is a nice extra signal that the noun is neuter and in its base form.

errorCorrection.explanation: The subject of a sentence stands in the nominative, the base dictionary form: Брат. Братом is a different case (instrumental) and cannot be the subject. Who lives in Moscow? Кто? — Брат.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: This is a school, not a library.
errorCorrection.explanation: After «Это» a noun is being named, so it stays in the nominative, its citation form: Это школа. Школу is the accusative form and does not fit here.

patternRecognition.question: Which ending rule makes журнал masculine?
options: It ends in a hard consonant
It ends in the soft sign -ь
patternRecognition.answer: It ends in a hard consonant
patternRecognition.explanation: Журнал ends in the hard consonant -л. The rule is: hard consonant → masculine.

patternRecognition.question: Which ending rule makes неделя feminine?
patternRecognition.explanation: Неделя ends in -я. Both -а and -я are the feminine endings; here it is -я. The two together make one of the three core rules.

patternRecognition.question: Which ending rule makes поле neuter?
patternRecognition.explanation: Поле ends in -е. The neuter rule covers both -о and -е together. Окно (in -о) and поле (in -е) are both neuter for the same reason.

categorySorting.instruction: Sort these nouns by gender. Read the last letter and apply the rule.

reviewVocab.definition: nominative case: the dictionary form of a noun. Used for the subject of a sentence; answers кто? or что?.
reviewVocab.example: Это книга. (Книга is in the nominative.)

reviewVocab.definition: grammatical gender. Every Russian noun is one of three: мужской, женский, or средний. Fixed and built into the word.
reviewVocab.example: Дом — мужской, книга — женский, окно — средний.

reviewVocab.definition: Hard consonant → M; -а / -я → F; -о / -е → N. The soft sign -ь is covered in lesson 2.
reviewVocab.example: Стол → M. Школа → F. Море → N.
